findings.what: It puts the maker's 'operation within 1 hour at 1.45 In' next to the slides' 'it can take 10,000 s' (2.8 h) and then says 'the cable must take that current for that long', without saying the two times disagree or which one the cable is designed for. Teach it as the sources differing: the maker's conventional time for breakers up to 63 A is 1 h, and the slides give a longer 10,000 s (p.30). The fact-checker's note asked for the same.

findings.where: Screen 9 (Section A (e) and (f)) and the Keep this card's showroom figures
findings.what: The 1.5 mm² answer depends on the 90 °C rating. Table 4E1A note 1 (his copy p.458) says to rate the cables at the lower temperature when the starter's or motor's terminals are designed for less than 90 °C. At 70 °C, Table 4D1A column 5 (his copy p.448) gives 1.5 mm² only 15.5 A, which no longer covers 16.66 A. This caveat appears only in the 'What this model ignores' panel, so a card meant for a real job shows 1.5 mm² with no warning. Add one line under (f) and a trap on the card.

'A full answer makes any three' lets the three hazard points (heat, damage to insulation and joints, fire) count as a full answer, even though the question's second half (how the design keeps a small overload from harming the cable, points 4 and 5) is left unanswered. Set need to a hazard plus at least one design point, e.g. 'any three, with at least one of points 4 and 5'.

findings.where: Screen 6 (Worked example), the note after the last line
findings.what: 'Your slides print 21.2 A, 19.3 A and 14.5 A, cut short rather than rounded' is true only of 21.2 A (21.28 A to one place is 21.3 A). 19.3 A is 19.34 A rounded correctly, and 14.5 A is exact. Say only 21.2 A is cut short.

findings.where: Screen 4 (overload picture), status line and mark labels during the demonstration and on any change
findings.what: The status line and the I2 and Iz label figures switch the moment the device or Cf changes, but the marks take 0.9 s to glide. So 'Fails' shows before I2's mark has passed 1.45 Iz, and 'Passes with Iz 13.79 A' shows while the I2 mark and the gap are still red. The film's red pixels confirm the red text and the red mark are out of step by about 0.6 s at each change. Switch the words when the marks arrive.

'A thermal relay is not one of the devices for which I2 ≤ 1.45 Iz is taken as met' refers to a list no screen gives: Regulation 433.1.201, under which BS EN 60898 breakers and BS 88 fuses meet it once Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz (source 51). State it once, on screen 4 where the breaker passes, and as a line in the card's rule.

'Set to 0.58 × the motor's In … That setting is the In of the starter-to-motor cables' uses In for two different things in back-to-back sentences. Call the first one the motor's full-load (nameplate) current.

refresher.md promised part (c) as 'the device and its rating', but the type is told after the typed rating rather than asked. A B, C or D choice set against the 62.32 A practice start (75, 125, 250 A) would make him choose it, and the feedback could say honestly that B also clears the start but with little room.
The catalogue quote is for type C and D breakers, while the picture's device is the slides' 10 A type B. Quote the same catalogue's type B row if it has one, so the time fits the device on screen.

findings.where: Screen 1 (Do you still have it?), the question
findings.what: 'Never both in one place' all but tells him the factors do not act together, so the 24.18 A slip is hardly tested. The slides' own description (clipped direct, in trunking with another circuit, then through a cavity wall with 50 mm of insulation, p.26) would leave him to see it.

findings.where: Screen 3 (The why: the run in sections), notes under the picture
findings.what: The insulated-wall section names no reference method, so 'its reference method sets the column' leaves open which column the wall's 19.34 A is read against. One line saying the slides count only Methods B and C in this run (p.28) completes the step.

findings.where: Screen 3, the sentence under the picture
findings.what: 'The warm room and the other circuit together stop the cable shedding its heat' blurs two causes. The explanation has it right: the warm room starts the cable warmer, and the other circuit stops it shedding heat.

findings.where: Screen 9, after the size and Iz
findings.what: Iz 16.00 A is below the 25 A breaker at DBP2. One line saying the breaker now gives these cables fault protection only, which lesson 7 checks, would head off the obvious 'but In ≤ Iz fails' question.

findings.where: Keep this card, 'The showroom so far' tile for 1e
findings.what: 'Table 4E1A, column 5 (Reference Method B, 3 or 4 cables)' is set in the large monospace figure style and wraps to five heavy lines at 1280 px and three at 360 px. Use a shorter text for the figure, or the label style for text figures.

The contact sheet (3000 × 23,870 px) is illegible at the size it is shown, so the overload motion could be checked only by measuring its pixels. A sheet of cropped scene-and-status frames would let a reader see it.
